div.head: Quadr II Praef 3
div.ab: Unde tanta genti securitas, tanta bonorum omnium copia successit, ut, si uere rationis honestate regeretur, etatis auree pristina tempora conformaret.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 542 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)
div.ab: Hence such security, such abundance of all goods has come to the people that, if it were truly ruled by the honesty of reason, it would match the former times of the golden age.

note.seg: Lobgedichte auf Englands Lage und Reichthum lagen dem Richard von Cluny (bei Berger Bibl. école franç. d'Athènes 1879) schon vor; vgl. ferner Laurentius Dunelmensis ed. Raine (1880) p. 2; Delpit Documents franç. I cxciv; Hs. Oxford Corpus College 232; Anglia . . fertilior cornu, Copia sacra tuo! Neu. Archiv f. Gesch. (1876) I 601; vgl. III 25; Johann von Salisbury Policrat. VIII 7. Den Vortheil ihrer Insellage rühmen auch andere Engländer des 12. Jhs.

Poems in praise of England's situation and wealth were already known to Richard of Cluny (in Berger, Bibl. école franç. d'Athènes 1879); cf. further Laurence of Durham ed. Raine (1880) p. 2; Delpit, Documents franç. I cxciv; MS Oxford Corpus College 232; Anglia . . fertilior cornu, Copia sacra tuo! Neu. Archiv f. Gesch. (1876) I 601; cf. III 25; John of Salisbury, Policrat. VIII 7. Other Englishmen of the 12th century also praise the advantage of their island position
